decisions.reason: The requirements constrain different extensions and different allowed message sets: supported_groups in CH/EE versus supported_versions in CH/SH/HRR.
One checks the offered obfuscated_ticket_age value, while the other checks that server processing does not use that value.
Both require a server to ignore an unrecognized ClientHello extension and continue processing; the canonical requirement has direct primary-body normative evidence.
The PSK case forbids CertificateVerify, whereas the certificate-authentication case requires Certificate; the states and checked messages differ.
The Handshake discriminants and body types differ: certificate/Certificate versus new_session_ticket/NewSessionTicket.
One checks omission when certificate authentication is not used; the other checks presence when certificate-based key exchange is used.
The Handshake discriminants and body types differ: encrypted_extensions/EncryptedExtensions versus finished/Finished.
They map different ContentType values: handshake to 22 and application_data to 23.
They constrain different enum types with different encoded widths: AlertLevel to 255 and SignatureScheme to 0xFFFF.
The first specifically requires CertificateVerify for a certificate-authenticating client; the second additionally checks Certificate and ordering before Finished.
The same placement set applies to different extension fields, server_name and max_fragment_length.
One forbids a server CertificateVerify under PSK authentication; the other requires a client CertificateVerify for certificate authentication.
They map different ContentType values: alert to 21 and application_data to 23.
One applies to records containing ServerHello, while the other applies specifically to TLSCiphertext records.
Supporting secp256r1 key exchange and implementing signature_algorithms_cert are different implementation capabilities.
They assign different wire values to different CertificateType members: X509 to 0 and RawPublicKey to 2.
One checks integrity against modification; the other checks post-establishment confidentiality against disclosure.
The same extension is forbidden in different handshake messages: Certificate versus EncryptedExtensions.
They constrain different enum types and widths: NamedGroup to 0xFFFF and KeyUpdateRequest to 255.
Early-data acceptance compares different PSK-associated values: TLS version versus selected ALPN protocol.
One zero-pads a Diffie-Hellman shared secret; the other zero-pads a Diffie-Hellman public key value.
key_share has different extension_data types in ClientHello and HelloRetryRequest.
Supporting rsa_pkcs1_sha256 certificate signatures and implementing key_share are different capabilities.
Supporting rsa_pss_rsae_sha256 certificate signatures and implementing supported_versions are different capabilities.
The derivations use different labels and produce different secrets: client early traffic versus early exporter master.
Supporting rsa_pkcs1_sha256 certificate signatures and implementing supported_groups are different capabilities.
The Handshake discriminants and body types differ: end_of_early_data/EndOfEarlyData versus certificate/Certificate.
The Handshake discriminants and body types differ: client_hello/ClientHello versus encrypted_extensions/EncryptedExtensions.
The same placement set applies to different extension fields, max_fragment_length and supported_groups.
They cover opposite negotiated-version conditions and directions: forbid supported_versions before TLS 1.3 and require it for TLS 1.3.
They constrain certificate_request_context in different message types: CertificateRequest outside post-handshake authentication versus server Certificate.
They constrain different enum types and widths: SignatureScheme to 0xFFFF and KeyUpdateRequest to 255.
The Handshake discriminants and body types differ: server_hello/ServerHello versus encrypted_extensions/EncryptedExtensions.
One checks the mask-generation digest for an RSAE PSS scheme; the other checks the signed digest for a PSS-key PSS scheme.
They constrain different enum types, ExtensionType and NamedGroup, despite equivalent numeric maxima.
One checks the signed digest for an RSAE PSS scheme; the other checks the mask-generation digest for a PSS-key PSS scheme.
Supporting rsa_pss_rsae_sha256 for CertificateVerify and implementing supported_versions are different capabilities.
Supporting rsa_pkcs1_sha256 certificate signatures and implementing signature_algorithms are different capabilities.
They map different cipher suites to different wire values: TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256 to 0x1301 and TLS_AES_128_CCM_8_SHA256 to 0x1305.
Early-data acceptance compares different PSK-associated values: selected cipher suite versus selected ALPN protocol.
They constrain different vectors with different bounds: ClientHello.cipher_suites and ServerHello.extensions.
One checks the peer public key as the scalar-multiplication input; the other checks use of the multiplication result as the shared secret.
The figure markers select different traffic epochs and keys: handshake_traffic_secret versus application_traffic_secret_N.
The identical vector bounds apply to different fields and data types: DistinguishedName and KeyShareEntry.key_exchange.
One forbids server Certificate under PSK authentication; the other requires server CertificateVerify under certificate authentication.
They apply to complementary external-PSK hash states and require different actions: default absent hashes versus set defined hashes at establishment.
They reserve different, disjoint SignatureScheme value ranges.
The same bounds apply to different vectors and element interpretations: OID filter values versus client key shares.
They check length-delimited bodies in different record structures: TLSPlaintext.fragment versus TLSCiphertext.encrypted_record.
They reserve different, disjoint SignatureScheme value ranges.
One forbids a client Certificate when none was requested; the other requires it when certificate-based client authentication was requested.
The derivations use different secrets, labels, and transcript endpoints: server handshake traffic versus client application traffic.
They constrain different enum types, ExtensionType and SignatureScheme, despite equivalent numeric maxima.
They constrain different extensions and allowed message sets: pre_shared_key in CH/SH versus cookie in CH/HRR.
They constrain different enum types with different encoded widths: ExtensionType to 65535 and PskKeyExchangeMode to 255.
One requires presence of each recognized requested extension OID; the other separately requires all requested values for each recognized OID.
Supporting rsa_pss_rsae_sha256 certificate signatures and implementing key_share are different capabilities.
key_share has different extension_data types in HelloRetryRequest and ServerHello.
The first generally requires a Certificate response when requested; the second applies only when no suitable certificate exists and requires that response to be empty.
Supporting rsa_pss_rsae_sha256 certificate signatures and implementing supported_groups are different capabilities.
They check length consistency in different record structures: TLSPlaintext.fragment versus TLSCiphertext.encrypted_record.
The same HelloRetryRequest validation step checks different fields: legacy_compression_method and legacy_session_id_echo.
They apply to different records and require different legacy versions: initial ClientHello uses 0x0301, while ServerHello uses 0x0303.
The derivations use different secrets, labels, and transcript endpoints: client handshake traffic versus server application traffic.
The Handshake discriminants and body types differ: certificate_request/CertificateRequest versus key_update/KeyUpdate.
Supporting rsa_pss_rsae_sha256 certificate signatures and implementing signature_algorithms are different capabilities.
